note:
I'm talking about the UI seen in the screenshot.

Formerly, these used to generally use percentiles for the auto-scaling, but I had it changed to use screen-widths instead. This task asks you to reintroduce percentiles, but as an option which one can pick instead of screen-widths. Screen-widths should remain the default.

This ask applies to all settings which use screen-widths as the auto-scaling measure (roads, passenger rail, ferries, etc.)
reply:
Merged, publishing 9 Oct ~01:20. Every layer that auto-fits by screen widths (roads' scenic metrics, rail's and ferries' ranked metrics) now has a unit menu in its caption: "Auto-fit: the best [15] [screen widths ▾] …" or "… the best [20] [% ▾] of roads in view, full colour from the best [0.1] %". Screen widths stay the default. Percentiles are of line length in view, the same code as before the switch (it never left: Elevation and Grade use it). Kept in the link (`fu=p` for roads, a trailing `p` for rail and ferries); old links read as screen widths. Equalise, Lock, Full and Auto work with either. Screenshots: scratchpad/pct/shots/.

Your calls: the percentile defaults are the old saved ones (scenic best 20 % … 0.1 %; rail ride score 30 % … 0.2 %; other rail metrics 2–98; ferries 0–100, which reads oddly as "the busiest 100 %"). Keep them, or set others? And the unit is per layer, not per metric (as the screen-width numbers are).
text: Add option for percentile colouring ranges, where "screen-widths" is currently supported
